question: Prediction of MCI-to-AD conversion within 3 years/36 months (pMCI vs sMCI) in ADNI from baseline MRI. P-3 uses T1 MRI only; P-72's reported model fuses sMRI grey matter with FDG-PET (MRI channel shared) and it also reports an sMRI-only arm. The recorded P-72 figure (94.61%) is its AD vs NC accuracy; judged here on P-72's printed conversion figures.
metric: Accuracy with accuracy and AUC with AUC; both papers report both.

figures.P-72: 238 sMCI/151 pMCI, subject-level 70/15/15 split (about 57 test subjects per split), averaged over three splits. sMRI-only MAResNet18: 73.68% (42/57), Wilson 61.0-83.4%; AUC 0.721, Hanley-McNeil (22/35) SE=0.072 -> 0.580-0.862. Multimodal SPDFC(0.6): 77.19% (44/57), Wilson 64.8-86.2%; AUC 0.755 -> 0.620-0.890.
figures.P-3: 298 sMCI/295 pMCI (ADNI1/2, Wen et al. splits), 5-fold CV, CAAT ensemble: accuracy 74.61% (fold variance 0.002; no interval), Wilson on n=593 70.9-77.9%; AUC 0.780 (fold variance 0.003), Hanley-McNeil n1=295, n2=298: Q1=0.639, Q2=0.684, SE=sqrt([0.78*0.22+294*(0.639-0.608)+297*(0.684-0.608)]/(295*298))=0.019 -> 0.743-0.817.

matched_figure_check: P-72's sMRI-only arm is P-3's input condition (T1 MRI only), on the same 3-year horizon. Accuracy: 73.68% vs 74.61%, each inside the other's interval (two-sample z=0.15). AUC: P-72's 0.721 lies 0.022 below P-3's derived lower bound 0.743, while P-3's 0.780 lies inside P-72's 0.580-0.862 (z=0.79). P-72's multimodal model (77.19%, 0.755) lies inside P-3's intervals on both metrics and P-3's figures lie inside its. The matched figure reconciles the accuracy comparison almost exactly; on AUC it fails to reconcile only in one direction, because P-3's 593-subject interval is narrow.
performance_validity: Passes: no conversion figure near ceiling (P-72 77.19%/0.755, sMRI-only 73.68%/0.721; P-3 74.61%/0.780).

candidate_explanations.difference: Architecture: P-3's CAAT ensemble transfers class-activation attention from three source tasks; P-3's own plain 3D CNN on the same splits gives 70.84% and AUC 0.758, so architecture alone moves AUC by 0.022 within P-3.
Input representation: whole 3D T1 image (P-3) vs grey-matter map (P-72).
candidate_explanations.quote: using only whole 3D images of the brain and no other ancillary information

candidate_explanations.difference: Cohort selection and class balance: P-3 uses the Wen et al. ADNI1/2 benchmark (298/295); P-72 is restricted to subjects with paired baseline MRI and FDG-PET (238/151).
candidate_explanations.quote: The dataset consists of 298 sMCI and 295 pMCI participants retrieved from datasets ANDI1 and ADNI2.

candidate_explanations.difference: Validation design: 5-fold CV over 593 (P-3) vs three hold-out splits of about 57 subjects (P-72).
candidate_explanations.quote: We followed the same data split strategy to construct three different subsets with different test sets, the average of three classification accuracies is used as the final result.

candidate_explanations.difference: sMCI label: P-3 requires the diagnosis to remain MCI through 36 months; P-72 labels non-converters as sMCI without a stated follow-up minimum.
candidate_explanations.quote: if the patient’s diagnosis remained as MCI, we categorized him/her as sMCI.

reason: On P-72's printed conversion figures, the matched sMRI-only accuracies are essentially identical (73.68% vs 74.61%) and P-72's reported model agrees with P-3 on both metrics. The only crossing is the AUC of P-72's sMRI-only ablation (0.721), which lies outside P-3's narrow derived interval while P-3's 0.780 lies well inside P-72's (z=0.79). That meets the letter of condition 4 in one direction only, and condition 3 is met on AUC but not on accuracy, so this is the weakest of the borderline cases. No paper shows any candidate explanation to be sufficient.

quotes.quote: MCI subjects who developed AD within 3 years were labeled as pMCI and those who did not convert to AD were labeled as sMCI.
To evaluate the performance, we performed 5-fold cross-validation of the dataset.
The dataset consists of 298 sMCI and 295 pMCI participants
